basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 29.' and it opens '(Vers. 29.) Et sumpserunt Abram et Nachor sibi uxores. Nomen uxoris Abram, Sarai: et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 29.) Et sumpserunt Abram et Nachor sibi uxores. Nomen uxoris Abram, Sarai: et nomen uxoris Nachor, Melcha filia Aran. Pater autem Melchae, ipse est pater Jescae. Aran filius Thare, frater Abraham et Nachor, duas filias genuit, Melcham, et Sarai cognomento Jescan, δυώνυμον. E quibus Melcham accepit uxorem Nachor, et Sarai Abraham: necdum quippe inter patruos, et fratrum filias nuptiae fuerant lege prohibitae, quae in primis hominibus, etiam inter fratres et sorores initae sunt.
